item.title: Thad Matta Retires: The End of a Remarkable 502-Win Coaching Career at Butler
item.description:
Just days after Butler’s athletic director publicly stated that Thad Matta would return for another season, the longtime college basketball coach reversed course and announced his retirement on Monday. With 502 career wins across 21 seasons, Matta leaves the sidelines as one of the most accomplished coaches of his generation — but he is not leaving Butler entirely.

Key Takeaways

  • Thad Matta retires with a 502-223 career record spanning 21 seasons at Butler, Xavier, and Ohio State.
  • He will remain at Butler as Special Assistant to the President and Athletic Director.
  • Matta made 13 NCAA Tournament appearances, including two Final Fours and one national championship game.
  • Butler has begun a national search for a new head coach.
  • The retirement comes after a 16-16 overall and 7-13 Big East season for the Bulldogs.

Thad Matta’s Sudden Retirement Announcement

The timing caught many off guard. On Friday, March 13, Butler Athletic Director Grant Leiendecker tried to dispel swirling rumors about Matta’s future, publicly stating the coach would return for another year. The Butler Collegian even reported that Matta was set to come back.

item.title: Tyler Tanner's Record-Breaking Run: How Vanderbilt Stormed the SEC Tournament
item.description:
A program that was once an afterthought in the SEC just knocked off the conference’s top seed. And a record-breaking defensive performance was at the heart of it all.

Quick Summary: Vanderbilt’s Tyler Tanner delivered a historic defensive performance as the Commodores took down top-seeded Florida 91-74 to reach the SEC Tournament final. This followed a 75-68 upset over Tennessee in the quarterfinals. Tanner’s back-to-back performances have been described as record-breaking, putting Vanderbilt in position for a deep March Madness run.

item.title: Ohio State vs Michigan Basketball: Can the 8th-Seed Buckeyes Shock the Big Ten's Best?
item.description:
The stage is set for one of college basketball’s fiercest rivalries to take center court in Chicago. Ohio State, the 8th seed, will square off against top-seeded Michigan in the Big Ten Tournament quarterfinals on March 13, 2026, at the United Center, with tipoff scheduled for noon ET on Big Ten Network.

Michigan enters with a staggering 29-2 record and a 19-1 mark in Big Ten play, while Ohio State (21-11) had to claw past Iowa just to earn this matchup. The question everyone is asking: does Ohio State have any realistic path to an upset, or is Michigan simply too dominant?

item.title: WVU Basketball Big 12 Tournament: Mountaineers' NCAA Hopes on the Line
item.description:
WVU basketball needs a miracle run — and they know it. The seventh-seeded West Virginia Mountaineers enter the Big 12 Tournament at 18-13, sitting firmly on the outside of the NCAA Tournament bubble. Their only path to March Madness likely runs through Kansas City.

Key Takeaways

  • WVU enters the Big 12 Tournament as the 7th seed with an 18-13 record
  • The Mountaineers are off Joe Lunardi’s NCAA Tournament bubble
  • Key wins this season: Kansas, BYU, and Pitt (71-49)
  • Senior guard Honor Huff earned All-Big 12 Honorable Mention
  • WVU women’s basketball won the Big 12 title and may host NCAA games

WVU Basketball’s Roller-Coaster Season Under Ross Hodge

First-year head coach Ross Hodge has navigated a season full of extremes. The highs have been exhilarating — none more than a 71-49 demolition of rival Pitt that Hodge says he’ll “never forget for as long as I live.”
